title: Riemannian Ordinary Least Squares
claim: Inputs of different types are mapped into one shared tangent space, where a linear combination yields the predicted response.
layout: Left-to-right, scalar panel feeds a manifold panel, with a legend box below
description: A wide geometric diagram. At top left, a number line has a green segment from z_k to its mean z̄_k. A dark arrow labeled 'Map line segment to tangent vector' points down to a yellow tangent plane at Ȳ. A green vector there is labeled (z_k − z̄_k)v_k. A large arrow labeled 'ROLS in common tangent space' leads right to a curved manifold M. On the manifold, a yellow tangent plane at Ȳ holds the green scalar-derived vector and a blue transported vector α_j Γ(Log(X_j)). A red solid line and a dashed line mark the sum, ending at the red 'Predicted response Ŷ'. A blue parallel-transport curve runs to a second tangent plane at X̄_j, which links through a dashed exponential-map arc to the point X_j. A bordered legend at the bottom gives the symbols for manifold, tangent space, tangent vector, exponential map and parallel transport. Green marks scalar inputs, blue marks manifold inputs, and red marks the prediction.
caption: Geometric overview of ROLS. Each manifold predictor $X_j$ is log-mapped to $\Tan{\FM{X}_j}$ and parallel-transported to the common tangent space $\Tan{\FM{Y}}$, where it is weighted by the scalar coefficient $\alpha_j$. Each scalar predictor $z_k$ contributes a centered tangent direction $(z_k-\bar z_k)\,v_k$. The predicted response is $\hat Y=\Exp{\FM{Y}}\bigl(\sum_j\alpha_j u_j+\sum_k(z_k-\bar z_k)v_k\bigr)$, where $u_j$ is the transported predictor.
abstract: Many scientific responses take values in Riemannian manifolds, with predictors that are scalar- and/or manifold-valued. A regression analysis in such settings must provide accurate prediction with hypothesis testing for individual coefficients. Yet no current manifold-regression framework accommodates both predictor types and enables per-coefficient hypothesis tests. We propose Riemannian Ordinary Least Squares (ROLS) as a tangent space conditional-mean model, which is the ordinary least squares (OLS) analogue for Riemannian manifolds. ROLS is well-defined under an explicit injectivity condition that keeps the logarithm maps single-valued, with cut-locus conditions for branch-sensitive cases outside it. Within the local geometric setting it admits a closed-form estimator, an $O(n^{-1})$ excess prediction-error bound with explicit curvature bias, and asymptotic $t$- and Wald tests for individual coefficients. With synthetic simulations and three real-data case studies, ROLS is shown to be competitive with the state-of-the-art baselines. In addition, the per-coefficient tests agree with effects reported in literature. We envision ROLS to be a standard tool for manifold-valued regression with coefficient-level inference to support scientific discovery, which can be interpreted in the same way as Euclidean OLS. The source code is available at https://github.com/XiaoyuChenPub/ROLS.
